changelog: [When to Segment]: broadened the conditional-ending rule to cover non-past '-으면/-으면은' in addition to past '-았/었으면(은)'; broadened the '?'-boundary rule so it also permits segmenting before a trailing noun-phrase/list elaboration (not only purpose/reason clauses); broadened the leading-filler rule to explicitly cover chains of two or more repeated discourse markers/fillers; and added two new generalizable cues — a fronted temporal/locational adverbial or long temporal setup ending in a discourse marker like '이제' before a subordinate/main clause, and a completed '-고 나서' sequential clause before its main clause — targeting the critic's measured under-segmentation cases (question+list, conditional+result, adverbial+subordinate, filler chains) without touching [Never Segment], since this iteration's rejected predecessor changed both sections at once and over-corrected.

[Examples — Segment]: added four new illustrative example pairs (question+trailing NP, conditional+result clause, fronted temporal adverbial+subordinate clause chain, leading disfluency chain) to demonstrate the newly broadened/added rules, keeping the section at the 12-example cap.
